items.title: Indecomposable projectives correspond to indecomposable Soergel modules
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and work in a regular integral type-A block over
$\mathbb C$. With the page's right wall-crossing convention and left
$C$-module values of $V$, there is an equivalence
$$V\colon\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\sim}\{\text{ungraded Soergel modules }B\otimes_S\mathbb C\},\qquad P(w\cdot\lambda)\longmapsto\bar B_{w^{-1}}.$$
The target is the additive category of direct summands of the right reductions
of polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodules, or equivalently of iterated
$C\otimes_{C^s}(-)$ applied to the trivial module $\mathbb C$, not to the
regular module $C$. For $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, the projective is the unique new
top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$; applying
$V$ gives the new summand of $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, thus the
inverse label. These normalized indecomposable polynomial lifts supply
self-dual auxiliary gradings; in rank one the centered degrees are $-1,1$,
with degrees $0,2$ after an uncentered shift. Forgetting grading recovers the
projective dictionary. More generally the ungraded equivalence with
Weyl-group Soergel modules holds for every complex semisimple regular integral
block; the type-A diagrammatic label comparison applies only in type A.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 At a height-one root prime $p$ with $T=R_p$, a two-label component has the upper projective $P_a=\Delta_T(a)$ and the pair projective $P_b$; $\operatorname{Hom}(P_a,P_b)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,P_a)$ are free of rank one, the canonical inclusion $i$ generates the first, and choosing $j$ in the second lifting its nonzero residual map gives a nonzero nilpotent $ij$ on the residue while $ji=h$ vanishes modulo $p$ by the nonsplitness of the residual standard extension; $1$ and $ij$ are residually independent and form a $T$-basis of the order $\operatorname{End}(P_b)=Z=\{(u_a,u_b):u_a\equiv u_b\bmod\tau(\alpha^\vee)\}$ of [F3], in generic tuple coordinates $ij=(h,0)$ and the order has basis $(1,1),(\alpha,0)$ with $\alpha=\tau(\alpha^\vee)$, so $h$ is a unit times $\alpha$ and rescaling $j$ makes $ji=\alpha$; then $V_T=\operatorname{Hom}(P_b,-)$ sends $P_b$ to $Z$ and $P_a$ to the rank-one upper branch $T$, with $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(Z,Z)=Z$, $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(T,T)=T$, $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(Z,T)=T$ generated by the projection and $\operatorname{Hom}_Z(T,Z)=T(\alpha,0)$, and $V(j),V(i)$ are these generators. [F1, F3, algebra]

1.2 Here is the actual deformed wall map missing from the ordinary formula [F2]. Write $A=R\otimes_{R^W}R$ and $A^s=R^s\otimes_{R^W}R$, with the common right parameter. For the wall target, adjunction and $T_{\rm out}P_R^\nu=P_R^\lambda$ give $V_R^\nu T_{\rm on}\cong\operatorname{Res}_{A^s}^A V_R^\lambda$, including the $A^s$ action by the central inclusion in [F3]. The closed fiber of $T_{\rm on}P_R^\lambda$ is two copies of the singular antidominant projective: its projective-injective summands have antidominant socle, and its Verma flag has every singular standard twice. Lifting both maps of this decomposition by [F3] gives $T_{\rm on}P_R^\lambda\in\operatorname{add}(P_R^\nu)$. Its canonical evaluation by $V_R^\nu$ equals $A$ as an $(A^s,A)$-bimodule, by adjunction with $T_{\rm out}$; thus $T_{\rm on}P_R^\lambda=P_R^\nu\otimes_{A^s}A$ by the evaluation isomorphism on $\operatorname{add}(P_R^\nu)$. The opposite adjunction now gives $V_R^\lambda T_{\rm out}N\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{A^s}(A,V_R^\nu N)$. Choose a root coordinate $\alpha$ with $s\alpha=-\alpha$. Since $R=R^s\oplus\alpha R^s$, the coefficient-of-$\alpha$ map $\ell:R\to R^s$ has pairing matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ on $1,\alpha$, hence identifies $R$ with its $R^s$-dual. Extending the right parameter identifies $\operatorname{Hom}_{A^s}(A,-)$ with $A\otimes_{A^s}-$, including the left $A$ action. Consequently $V_R\theta_s\cong A\otimes_{A^s}V_R\cong R\otimes_{R^s}V_R$ by actual action-compatible maps. This argument uses adjunction and relative Frobenius duality, not an isomorphism of residues. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 For a polynomial Bott-Samelson bimodule $B$, $M=B\otimes_SR$ is finite free over the right $R$. A left denominator nonzero at the origin acts invertibly: modulo the right maximal ideal its constant plus positive-degree part is invertible, since positive left invariants annihilate the finite-dimensional coinvariant reduction and positive-degree operators there are nilpotent; Nakayama makes its matrix invertible over $R$. Both left and right actions therefore extend to $R$. Weyl invariants balance across every tensor factor, so these actions factor through $A$. Iterating the map in step 1.2 identifies the localized polynomial tensor word with $V_R$ of the deformed wall word, with empty word the identity graph $R=V_R\Delta_R(\lambda)$. All identifications preserve the generic tuple branches and the right parameter. The fixed average coordinate in the type-A permutation model is split off before this construction. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Let $Q,Q'$ be deformed block projectives. Their canonical comparison under $V_R$ is an isomorphism at every height-one prime. At nonroot primes, the distinct simple Verma components give one-label Morita equivalences; at root primes, each projective decomposes into the two elementary projectives of step 1.1 by lifting its actual residue decomposition with the projective Hom base-change maps in [F3], so that step verifies every pair of summands. The source Hom module is finite free over $R$ by [F3]. The target $\operatorname{Hom}_A(V_RQ,V_RQ')$ need not be assumed free in advance: it is the submodule of finite free $\operatorname{Hom}_R(V_RQ,V_RQ')$ satisfying the finitely many linear commutation equations for a finite $R$-basis of $A$. Inside the generic Hom space it is the intersection of its height-one localizations, since a rational matrix belongs to the free ambient matrix lattice precisely when all its height-one localizations do, and the $A$-linearity equations already hold generically. The coefficientwise UFD intersection argument of the central-action lemma gives the same intersection property for the source Hom lattice. Their height-one equalities therefore prove the comparison is an isomorphism over $R$; in particular the target is now free. This is full faithfulness on deformed projectives. [F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For polynomial Bott-Samelson modules $M,M'$ the module $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M')$ is the localization of the polynomial Hom module, and the composite $\operatorname{Hom}_A(M,M')\otimes_R\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_R}(Q_R,Q_R')\otimes_R\mathbb C\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(Q,Q')\cong\operatorname{Hom}_C(VQ,VQ')$ is the natural reduction map by step 3.1, projective Hom base change and the ordinary Struktursatz, all maps being the canonical composition maps; hence reduction-of-Hom holds for Bott-Samelson modules and, by taking summands, for all polynomial Soergel bimodules, the degree components giving the graded statement. [F1, F3, step 2.1, step 3.1]

5.1 Absolute complex extension follows by the actual same equations as real extension, not by a real-only assertion. For the rational $B_w$, write $E_{\mathbb Q}^0$ for its finite-dimensional local degree-zero endomorphism algebra and $J_{\mathbb Q}$ for its nilpotent radical; [F4] gives $E_{\mathbb Q}^0/J_{\mathbb Q}=\mathbb Q$. Fixed-degree maps are kernels of finite rational linear commutation equations on homogeneous generator images. Tensoring these equations with the flat field $\mathbb C$ identifies $E_{\mathbb C}^0=E_{\mathbb Q}^0\otimes_{\mathbb Q}\mathbb C$. Its ideal $J_{\mathbb Q}\otimes\mathbb C$ is nilpotent and its quotient is $\mathbb C$, so every element with nonzero scalar residue is invertible by a finite geometric series; hence this is a local algebra with residue $\mathbb C$. The same flat equations preserve its top graph and degree. Extending each rational word decomposition gives a complex decomposition into these absolutely indecomposable labels; finite Krull--Schmidt uniqueness then classifies every summand of every complex word. Thus the normalized polynomial $B_w$ has the required local degree-zero algebra over $\mathbb C$. Step 4.1 makes the degree-zero algebra of $\bar B_w$ its quotient, hence local. Here is the needed passage to ungraded endomorphisms. For the finite-dimensional graded algebra $E=\operatorname{End}(\bar B_w)$, grading scalings preserve its Jacobson radical $J$; interpolation in finitely many distinct scaling parameters extracts every homogeneous component, so $J$ is graded. The semisimple quotient $E/J$ is a product of matrix algebras by [F6]. Its grading derivation preserves each factor, since a derivation kills central idempotents. Every derivation $D$ of $\operatorname{Mat}_n(\mathbb C)$ is inner: with matrix units, $H=\sum_i D(e_{i1})e_{1i}$ satisfies $D(a)=Ha-aH$, by applying the product rule to $e_{ij}e_{k1}$ and summing in $k$. The grading derivation is diagonalizable; writing $H=H_s+H_n$ shows $\operatorname{ad}H_n=0$, because it is the commuting nilpotent part of $\operatorname{ad}H$. A scalar nilpotent matrix is zero, so $H$ is semisimple up to an irrelevant scalar. Its degree-zero centralizer is consequently a product of matrix algebras on its eigenspaces. Thus $(E/J)_0$ is semisimple. It is a quotient of the local $E_0$, so it equals $\mathbb C$; a product of such centralizers can have dimension one only if there is a single matrix factor of size one. Hence $E/J=\mathbb C$, and $E$ is local. This proves that $\bar B_w$ remains indecomposable after forgetting grading; it supplies the graded-algebra argument rather than attributing innerness to Wedderburn-Artin. [F4, F6, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 The normalized top summand is self-dual without assuming an unproved indecomposable-form assertion. In the unshifted tensor ring of a length-$k$ word, each added reflection factor is a quadratic finite free extension with basis $1,\alpha_s$ and relation $\alpha_s^2\in S^s$. The coefficient-of-$\alpha_s$ functional has perfect pairing matrix $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$; composing these functionals along the tensor tower gives a perfect right-$S$ pairing on its rank-$2^k$ basis. It is left-invariant by commutativity of the tensor ring. The total trace has degree $-2k$, so shifting the word by $(k)$ gives a degree-zero isomorphism from the Bott-Samelson bimodule to its invariant right dual $D B=\operatorname{Hom}_S(B,S)$. For a reduced word of $w$, $B_w$ is the unique summand with nonzero top graph $w$, of generic right rank one there; all other summands have strictly lower graph support by [F4]. Duality preserves generic graph branches: a left scalar on a rank-one branch acts by the same scalar on its right dual. Therefore $D B_w$ is an indecomposable summand of the very same self-dual word, has its $w$ branch, and must be the identical unique top summand, with no shift. Thus $B_w\cong D B_w$. Finite right projectivity makes duality commute with right origin reduction, so $\bar B_w$ has a graded self-duality centered at zero. Any two finite graded lifts with the same indecomposable underlying $C$-module differ by a shift: homogeneous components of an ungraded isomorphism and its inverse give $1=\sum_d g_{-d}f_d$ in the local degree-zero endomorphism algebra; one summand is a unit, so $f_d$ is an isomorphism after a shift (its source and target have the same finite dimension). A nonzero shift cannot preserve centered self-duality, by symmetry of the extreme degrees. This proves unique centered normalization; rank one has degrees $-1,1$, and an uncentered shift gives $0,2$. [F4, F5, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Induction on Bruhat length gives the label dictionary: for a reduced word $w=s_1\cdots s_k$, $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique new top-label summand of $\theta_{s_k}\cdots\theta_{s_1}\Delta(\lambda)$ by [F2], and applying $V$ and the iterated wall-crossing formula gives the new summand of the reduced left tensor word $\overline{B_{s_k}\cdots B_{s_1}}$, whose top graph label is the inverse $w^{-1}$, while every proper subexpression contributes already-matched smaller labels; full faithfulness of step 3.1 for the deformed side and the indecomposability of step 5.1 match the two new summands uniquely, so $VP(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\bar B_{w^{-1}}$, and distinct labels remain non-isomorphic because $V$ is fully faithful on projectives. [F2, step 3.1, step 5.1]

7.1 The type-A equivalence and normalized dictionary follow from steps 4.1 through 6.2. For a semisimple product of type-A factors, reflection words reorder into the independent factor words and their reductions are tensor products of the factor reductions. Their endomorphism algebra is the tensor product of the finite factor endomorphism algebras: in finite bases, the commutation equations for the two independent coefficient algebras give this tensor-Hom identity. Each factor algebra is local with residue $\mathbb C$ by step 5.1; the sum of its tensor-extended radicals is nilpotent and its quotient is $\mathbb C$, so the product reduction is indecomposable. The labels, inverse convention and centered self-duality therefore combine factorwise; a rank-zero factor contributes the unit. The ungraded equivalence for every complex semisimple type needs no unprovided diagrammatic classification: define its Weyl-group Soergel-module category as the additive category of summands of polynomial Bott-Samelson right reductions. For every reflection realization, $S=S^s\oplus\alpha_sS^s$, and Weyl invariants balance across the tensor factors; the elementary quotient computation gives $B_s\otimes_SC=(C\otimes_{C^s}C)(1)$ exactly as in the wall-crossing theorem. Thus forgetting shifts identifies all right-reduced words with the ordinary $V$-images of wall words starting at $V\Delta(\lambda)=\mathbb C$. Ordinary full faithfulness [F1] lifts every idempotent between these images uniquely to an idempotent of their projective words. Since all projectives occur as summands of such words by [F2], this is a fully faithful and essentially surjective equivalence in every type. Its indecomposable labels can be read from the unique new projective summands themselves. The additional type-A polynomial/diagrammatic label and centered self-dual normalization are exactly those established in steps 5.1 through 6.2; no type-A classification is substituted for a general-type classification. [F1, F2, F4, step 4.1, step 6.1, step 6.2, algebra] ∎

items.title: Verma-flag multiplicities are standard-filtration ranks under V
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a projective $P$ in a regular integral type-A
block, choose its polynomial Soergel lift $\mathsf B(P)$ determined by the
preceding projective dictionary: if $P=\bigoplus_wP(w\cdot\lambda)^{m_w}$, take
$\mathsf B(P)=\bigoplus_wB_{w^{-1}}^{m_w}$, so that its right reduction is
$V(P)$ after forgetting auxiliary grading. Write $r_{x,d}(\mathsf B(P))$ for
the graded multiplicity of the polynomial standard graph module supported at
$x$ in its standard support filtration, with the standard-generator
normalization of the polynomial Soergel category. Then
$$(P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_d r_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P)).$$
Equivalently the polynomial Soergel character of this lift, evaluated at $v=1$
and with inverse labels, recovers the ordinary Verma-flag character of $P$.
These are ranks before reduction; no separated Bruhat-support filtration
intrinsic to the finite-dimensional module $V(P)$ is asserted, since the graph
supports coalesce at the origin. The same ungraded multiplicity comparison
holds with the corresponding Weyl-group polynomial/deformed lifts in other
complex semisimple types.
items.strategy:
**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 The functor $V_R$ is exact and sends each deformed standard $\Delta_R(y\cdot\lambda)$ to a finite free $R$-module of rank one: by [F4] its closed fiber is one-dimensional, and by [F2] the Hom module into the Verma-filtered standard is finite free with base change, so the rank is one. [F2, F4]

1.2 On that rank-one free module the center acts on the generic constituent of highest weight $y\cdot\lambda+\tau$ by the scalar $\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z)(y(\lambda+\rho)+\tau)=\sigma_\lambda(\operatorname{HC}_\rho(z))(y^{-1}\tau)$, which in the polynomial graph convention [F3] is the branch of the graph label $x=y^{-1}$; hence the graph label of the standard constituent is the inverse of its highest-weight label. [F2, F3]

1.3 The preceding dictionary proves the deformed, action-compatible wall isomorphism $V_R\theta_s\cong R\otimes_{R^s}V_R$ by adjunction, the translated central inclusion and the coefficient-of-$\alpha_s$ Frobenius pairing; it also proves deformed full faithfulness and the natural reduction-of-Hom map. Iteration identifies the localized polynomial word with the $V_R$-image of its lifted projective word. The unique top-label polynomial summand and the top projective summand match under this full faithfulness, by the dictionary's length induction. Restriction to their matching idempotents therefore gives an actual $A$-module isomorphism $\mathsf B(P)\otimes_SR\cong V_RP_R$, preserving every generic branch. It is not inferred from a mere origin isomorphism. [F1, F2, F3, algebra]

2.1 Passing to the fraction field, the graph-support ranks of $\mathsf B(P)$ at $x$ are therefore the multiplicities of the deformed Verma constituents of $P_R$ at the inverse label $y=x^{-1}$, and flat localization preserves these ranks; the deformed Verma flag of $P_R$ specializes exactly to the Verma flag of $P$ by [F2], so summing the graded multiplicities gives $(P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_dr_{y^{-1},d}(\mathsf B(P))$, which is the stated comparison at $v=1$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3]

3.1 These are ranks before origin reduction, so no intrinsic separated support filtration on $V(P)$ is asserted. For another complex semisimple type use the deformed lift $V_RP_R$ and its generic branch ranks, constructed in the preceding dictionary without type-A diagrammatic classification. Steps 1.1--1.2 identify each standard with its rank-one inverse branch in any reflection realization, so the same equality holds for these Weyl-group deformed lifts; whenever a corresponding polynomial lift is chosen, its localization has those same ranks. The type-A polynomial support-filtration formula is the particular case of step 2.1, with the fixed average coordinate split off. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_2 and S_3 as graded regular representations
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. We
work over $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$ and compute the coinvariant algebra of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] in the two smallest
cases and read off its graded decomposition, checking the general theorem
[[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]]; the
example is a verification in small rank and is not used as evidence for the
general statement.

**The case $W=S_2$.** Here $r=1$, the auxiliary polynomial ring is
$\mathbb k[x]$ with the transposition acting by $x\mapsto-x$, and the basic invariant is $x^2$, so
$$C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$$ with $\deg x=2$ in the page normalization and
$\deg x=1$ for the classical Hilbert series. The Hilbert series is therefore
$1+t^2$ in page degrees (equivalently $1+t$ in classical degrees), agreeing
with $\prod_i(1+t^2+\cdots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$ for the single basic degree $d_1=2$
of [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]]. The
degree-zero piece $C_0=\mathbb k$ is the trivial representation, and the
one-dimensional top piece $C_2=\mathbb k x$ is the sign representation, so $C$
is the regular representation of $S_2$ with graded multiplicities one for the
trivial and one for the sign module.

**The case $W=S_3$.** Use the auxiliary permutation model of
[[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]:
$$C=\mathbb k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3),\qquad e_1=x_1+x_2+x_3,\ e_2=x_1x_2+x_1x_3+x_2x_3,\ e_3=x_1x_2x_3,$$
with $S_3$ permuting the variables. In classical degrees the basic degrees are
$1,2,3$, so the Hilbert series is
$$\frac{(1-t)(1-t^2)(1-t^3)}{(1-t)^3}=(1+t)(1+t+t^2)=1+2t+2t^2+t^3,$$
and in the page normalization, where each variable has degree $2$, it becomes
$(1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4)=1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$. The graded pieces have dimensions
$1,2,2,1$ in degrees $0,2,4,6$.

**Graded pieces as $S_3$-modules.** Identify $C$ with the coinvariant algebra of
the two-dimensional reflection representation $\mathfrak h\subset\mathbb k^3$.
The degree-zero piece $C_0$ is the trivial module. The degree-two piece $C_2$
is spanned by the images of $x_1,x_2,x_3$ modulo $e_1$; these span a
two-dimensional space on which $S_3$ acts as the standard reflection
representation. Put $a=x_1$, $b=x_2$, $x_3=-a-b$. The relations are
$a^2+ab+b^2=0$ and $a^2b+ab^2=0$, so $b^3=0$ and
$C_6$ is spanned by the nonzero class $ab^2$ (its nonvanishing also follows
from the Hilbert series). The Vandermonde reduces to $-6ab^2$, so it spans
$C_6$ and carries the sign character. The perfect multiplication pairing
$C_2\times C_4\to C_6$ from
[[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]]
identifies $C_4$ with $C_2^*\otimes\mathrm{sign}$. The standard reflection
representation is self-dual: the invariant coordinate dot product restricts
nondegenerately to the sum-zero plane. Hence $C_4$ is standard tensor sign. Thus
$$C_0=\text{trivial},\quad C_2=\text{standard},\quad C_4=\text{standard}\otimes\text{sign},\quad C_6=\text{sign},$$
the graded lift of the regular representation, with graded multiplicities
$1$ for the trivial module, $t^6$ for the sign module and $t^2+t^4$ for the
two-dimensional standard module.

**Character check.** By
[[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]] the
graded character is
$$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}.$$
For a transposition in $S_3$ the eigenvalues on $\mathfrak h^*$ are $1,-1$, so
$\det(1-t^2w)=(1-t^2)(1+t^2)=1-t^4$ and the quotient is
$(1-t^4)(1-t^6)/(1-t^4)=1-t^6$, matching the direct sum
$1+0\cdot t^2+0\cdot t^4+(-1)t^6$. For a three-cycle the eigenvalues are the
primitive cube roots $\omega,\omega^2$, so $\det(1-t^2w)=1+t^2+t^4$ and the
quotient is $(1-t^4)(1-t^6)/(1+t^2+t^4)=(1-t^2)(1-t^4)=1-t^2-t^4+t^6$, matching
$1+(-1)t^2+(-1)t^4+t^6$. At $w=1$ the quotient is
$1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$ and its value at $t=1$ is $6=|S_3|$. In both cases the
graded character at $t=1$ is the character of the regular representation, and
the sum of graded multiplicities times dimensions is
$1+2+2+1=6=|W|$, respectively $1+1=2=|S_2|$, as the general theorem asserts.
items.strategy: Direct computation of the quotient by the basic invariants in the given coordinates; the Hilbert series is [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] with the basic degrees $1,2$ (respectively $1,2,3$); the identification of the graded pieces with the named $S_n$-modules is by comparing characters at the transpositions and the three-cycle, and the conclusion is the general theorem. The example is a verification of the general statement in the smallest cases and is not used as evidence for it.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor on Verma modules in rank one
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Work in $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ with the conventions of
[[def-bgg-category-o]]: $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, so the regular standards are
$\Delta_1=M(0)$ and $\Delta_s=M(-2)$ for the two elements of
$W=\{1,s\}$, and the singular wall weight is $\mu=-1$, whose shifted value is
$\mu+\rho=0$. The dominant regular integral block is that of $\lambda=0$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]), and
the wall-crossing functor is that of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] built from the two-dimensional
translating module $E=L(1)$ with highest weight $\mu-\lambda=-1$ up to Weyl
conjugacy.

**Onto the wall.** Tensoring the two regular standards with the two-dimensional
module and projecting to the central character of the wall preserves the
unique wall standard: $T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta_1\cong M(-1)$ and
$T_{\mathrm{on}}\Delta_s\cong M(-1)$, since $\Delta_1$ and $\Delta_s$ differ by
the single simple-root lowering and the tensor filtration retains exactly the
labels of weight $-1$ in the shifted parametrization, as in
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]].

**Back out of the wall.** The wall block at $\mu=-1$ has a single simple
object $M(-1)=L(-1)$ and is semisimple; hence $M(-1)$ is projective and
injective there, and the exact biadjoint return translation
$T_{\mathrm{out}}$ sends it to a projective object of the regular block whose
Verma flag has the two factors $M(0)$ and $M(-2)$, once each, by
[[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]]. By biadjunction, its Hom to $L(-2)$ is one-dimensional, since
$T_{\mathrm{on}}L(-2)=M(-1)$; its Hom to $L(0)$ is zero, since
$L(1)\otimes L(0)=L(1)$ has a different central character from $M(-1)$.
Thus its only simple quotient is $L(-2)$, once, and the projective-cover
decomposition identifies it with $P(-2)$.

**Conclusion.** Both $\theta_s\Delta_1$ and $\theta_s\Delta_s$ are therefore
isomorphic to the same nonsplit two-step extension
$$0\longrightarrow M(0)\longrightarrow P(-2)\longrightarrow M(-2)\longrightarrow 0,$$
with class $[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]$ in the Grothendieck group, in agreement with
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]].
Maximal-weight peeling puts $M(0)$ first in the flag; the extension is
nonsplit because $P(-2)$ is indecomposable as a projective cover. The wall
sits at highest weight $-1$, equivalently at shifted parameter $\mu+\rho=0$;
the regular highest weight $0$ is the dominant maximum of the block;
the antidominant minimum is $-2$.
items.strategy: Apply the extremal-weight tensor filtration to the natural two-dimensional module and project to the indicated central character. There is one retained wall standard and two retained return standards. The return is projective because M(-1) is the projective simple in its one-simple block and return translation is exact biadjoint. Its once-each flag and antidominant simple quotient identify it with P(-2). Maximal-weight peeling puts M(0) first; nonsplitting follows from indecomposability of that cover. The zero wall is the shifted parameter mu+rho, not the regular highest weight0.

items.title: The class map and the wall-crossing action in rank two
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. Work in
type $A_2$: the Weyl group is $W=S_3=\langle s,t\rangle$ with $s^2=t^2=1$ and
$m_{st}=3$, so that the six elements $1,s,t,st,ts,sts$ are distinct, with
$sts=tst=w_0$. Fix a dominant regular integral weight $\lambda$ and its regular
integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ in the sense of
[[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], with
standards $\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)$ indexed by $v\in W$. By
[[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] the classes
$[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]$ form a $\mathbb Z$-basis of $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$,
so the assignment
$$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad c[\Delta(v\cdot\lambda)]=v$$
is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]]
identifies the class action of the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] with right multiplication by
$1+s$, and likewise for $t$.

**The two-step products.** Applying the class formula first to
$\Delta(\lambda)$ and then to the one-step object gives
$$c\,[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+s)(1+t)=1+s+t+st,$$
because $\theta_s$ acts first and contributes the factor $1+s$ on the right.
The other order gives
$$c\,[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=(1+t)(1+s)=1+t+s+ts.$$
Thus
$$[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$$
while
$$[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)]=[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)].$$

**Non-commutativity.** The two products differ: the coefficients of the
length-two elements $st$ and $ts$, which are distinct elements of $S_3$, are
interchanged. Since the Verma classes are linearly independent, the two class
operators on $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ differ, and in fact they already differ
on the single class $[\Delta(\lambda)]$. This is the same non-commutativity as
in the Hecke algebra of the $S_3$ system, whose standard generators satisfy
$T_sT_t=T_{st}\ne T_{ts}=T_tT_s$; the wall-crossing functors accordingly
behave Hecke-like rather than like a commuting tuple of group elements, and the
two-step products are already sensitive to the order in which the walls are
crossed.

**Projective multiplicities.** The object $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)$ is
projective, and its class contains the single Bruhat-maximal label $ts$ with
coefficient one. By
[[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]
for the reduced word $ts$ (the composite $\theta_s\theta_t$ applies $\theta_t$
first), the indecomposable projective $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$ occurs as a summand
of $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta(\lambda)$ with multiplicity one, and every other
indecomposable summand has a strictly smaller label, i.e. lies among
$P(1),P(s\cdot\lambda),P(t\cdot\lambda)$. The multiplicity of $P(ts\cdot\lambda)$
is read off from the unitriangularity of the standard-support matrix of the
block; the remaining multiplicities are determined recursively but the example
records only the top one.
items.strategy: Read off the class formula from [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] applied first to $\Delta_1$ and then to the two-factor objects; the two computations differ in the label of the length-two factor ($ts$ versus $st$), which are distinct elements of $S_3$ and hence distinct Verma classes by the standard basis theorem [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]. The projective multiplicities follow from [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]] for the word ts (since theta_s theta_t applies t first), with the corrected standard-support triangle y<=x of the Verma-flag matrix.

items.title: Wall-crossing functors do not commute
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type
$A_2$ with distinct simple reflections $s,t$ (so $m_{st}=3$), the wall-crossing
functors $\theta_s\theta_t$ and $\theta_t\theta_s$ on the regular integral block
commute, so that the assignment $s\mapsto\theta_s$ defines a representation of
$W=S_3$ on the block. This is false: the two functors are not naturally
equivalent, and $\theta_s^2$ is not the identity.

items.title: Wall-crossing on the projectives in the sl_2 block
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. Work in the regular integral
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block with $\lambda=0$, $\rho=1$, so $s\cdot0=-2$ and the
singular wall weight is $\mu=-1$ with $\mu+\rho=0$. The indecomposable
projectives are $P_e=M(0)=\Delta_e$ and $P_s=P(-2)$, whose Verma flag is
$\Delta_e,\Delta_s$ with each standard once
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]],
[[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]).

Set $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$.

**On the standards.** By
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]]
the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of
[[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies
$\theta_s\Delta_e=\theta_s\Delta_s=P_s$, the nonsplit two-step extension of
$\Delta_s$ by $\Delta_e$: the one-letter reduced word
$w=s$ gives $\theta_s\Delta(\lambda)=P(s\cdot\lambda)$ as its unique new
summand, and the flag computation $\Delta_e+\Delta_s$ shows the summand is the
whole object.

**On the projectives.** Exactness of $\theta_s$
([[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]]) applied
to the flag $0\to\Delta_e\to P_s\to\Delta_s\to0$ shows that $\theta_sP_s$ has
standard flag multiplicities $(\Delta_e,\Delta_s)=(2,2)$. Every projective in
this two-simple block is a direct sum of copies of $P_e$ and $P_s$, whose flag
multiplicities are $(1,0)$ and $(1,1)$ by BGG reciprocity
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]); writing $\theta_sP_s\cong
P_e^{\oplus a}\oplus P_s^{\oplus b}$, the equations $a+b=2$ and $b=2$ give
$a=0$, $b=2$, so
$$\theta_sP_e\cong P_s,\qquad \theta_sP_s\cong P_s\oplus P_s.$$
In the ordered projective bases $(P_e,P_s)$, with columns indexed by the input,
the matrix of $\theta_s$ is therefore $\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$.
On the Soergel side $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$ with $\deg x=2$, $C^s=\mathbb k$,
$V(P_e)=\mathbb k$ and $V(P_s)=C$; the wall-crossing theorem
[[thm-wall-crossing-under-the-soergel-functor-is-tensoring-with-the-coinvariant-soergel-bimodule]]
gives
$$V\theta_s(P_e)=C\otimes_{C^s}\mathbb k\cong C,\qquad V\theta_s(P_s)=C\otimes_{C^s}C\cong C\oplus C$$
as left $C$-modules, the left $C$-acting on the first factor, and the
projective Struktursatz
[[thm-soergels-struktursatz-full-faithfulness-on-projectives]] reflects these
isomorphisms back to the projective identities above, all objects involved
being projective.

**Dimension comparison.** The tensor $C\otimes_{C^s}C\cong C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$
is the four-dimensional coinvariant bimodule $=2|W|$ with $|W|=2$, explicitly
spanned by the four elements $1\otimes1,1\otimes x,x\otimes1,x\otimes x$; the
isomorphism $C\oplus C\to C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$ of left $C$-modules sends
$(u,v)$ to $u\otimes1+v\otimes x$. By contrast the right-reduced polynomial
$B_s=\mathbb k[a]\otimes_{\mathbb k[a^2]}\mathbb k[a](1)$ is only
two-dimensional, with generator degrees $-1,1$ after centering; the right-reduced polynomial module is $C(1)$, whereas the
coinvariant bimodule $C\otimes_{\mathbb k}C$ has dimension four. The former
models $V\theta_s(P_e)$ and the latter the tensor operator applied to
$V(P_s)=C$.
items.strategy: For the first equality, apply the existing projective-generation and two-step wall-extension lemmas to the one-letter reduced word: theta_s M(0)=P(-2), with standard flag M(0),M(-2). For the second equality, exact biadjoint translation preserves projectives. Apply theta_s to the flag 0→M(0)→P_s→M(-2)→0. Its two outer values are P_s by the existing rank-one two-step extension, so theta_s P_s has standard multiplicities (2,2). Every projective in this two-simple block is a sum of P_e and P_s, whose flags have multiplicities (1,0),(1,1) by BGG reciprocity. The equations a+b=2 and b=2 give a=0,b=2, proving the object isomorphism without treating a class identity as an isomorphism by itself. Alternatively compute with the existing wall-crossing-under-V theorem: s(x)=-x gives C^s=k; the left C-linear isomorphism C⊕C→C⊗_k C sends (u,v) to u⊗1+v⊗x. The projective Struktursatz reflects this isomorphism because all objects concerned are projective. Display both tensor basis and projective multiplicity calculation; no generated B item is a dependency.

items.title: The Soergel functor on the small regular sl_2 block
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice inherited from the category-$\mathcal O$ suppliers.
Work in the dominant regular integral $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block at $\lambda=0$,
with $\rho=1$, $W=\{e,s\}$ and $s\cdot0=-2$
([[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]]). Set $\mathbb k=\mathbb C$. Put
$\Delta_e=M(0)$, $\Delta_s=M(-2)=L(-2)$, $P_e=P(0)=\Delta_e$ and $P_s=P(-2)$;
the block is described by the nonsplit sequences
$$0\to L(-2)\to\Delta_e\to L(0)\to0,\qquad 0\to\Delta_e\to P_s\to\Delta_s\to0,$$
the second being the one-letter case of
[[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]]
and [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]],
and $P_e=\Delta_e$ being the dominant Verma
([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[def-verma-module]]).

**The values of $V$.** Let $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$ with $\deg x=2$ be the
coinvariant algebra and $V=\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,-)$
([[def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-soergel-functor]]), so that
$\operatorname{End}(P_s)\cong C$ by
[[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]].
Since $P_s$ has indecomposable head $L(-2)$ and $L(-2)=M(-2)$ is simple, the
left $C$-module values are
$$V(P_e)=\mathbb k=C/(x),\quad V(P_s)=C,\quad V(\Delta_e)=V(\Delta_s)=\mathbb k,\quad V(L(0))=0,\quad V(L(-2))=\mathbb k.$$
Indeed $V(\Delta_e)$ and $V(\Delta_s)$ are one-dimensional by exactness applied
to the first sequence and $V(L(-2))=\mathbb k$ from the head quotient, while
$V(L(0))=0$ because $L(0)$ is not a quotient of $P_s$; the unique
one-dimensional $C$-module is $\mathbb k$ with $x$ acting by zero.

**The projective Hom table.** With rows indexed by the source and columns by the
target, the four Hom spaces in the ordered bases $(P_e,P_s)$ are
$$\begin{pmatrix}\operatorname{Hom}(P_e,P_e)&\operatorname{Hom}(P_e,P_s)\\\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,P_e)&\operatorname{Hom}(P_s,P_s)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}\mathbb k&\mathbb k\\\mathbb k&C\end{pmatrix},\qquad\text{dimensions }\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&2\end{pmatrix}.$$
Choose the nonzero maps $i\colon P_e\to P_s$ and $p\colon P_s\to P_e$; under the
Struktursatz [[thm-soergels-struktursatz-full-faithfulness-on-projectives]]
their images in $\operatorname{Hom}_C(\mathbb k,C)=\mathbb k\,i_0$ and
$\operatorname{Hom}_C(C,\mathbb k)=\mathbb k\,p_0$ are the generators
$i_0(1)=x$ and $p_0(a+bx)=a$, and the compositions compute
$p_0i_0=0$ on $\mathbb k$ while $i_0p_0=m_x$, multiplication by $x$ on $C$
(equivalently $pi=0$ and $ip$ is a nonzero square-zero
endomorphism; rank one refers to its image under $V$ on $C$). In particular $\operatorname{End}(P_s)\cong C$ is
recovered as the full two-dimensional endomorphism algebra, and the
full-faithfulness comparison is computed on the four projective Hom spaces
rather than claimed for the whole block.

**Polynomial lifts and standard ranks.** For $S=\mathbb k[a]$ with
$s(a)=-a$, the empty-word lift is $B_e=S$ and the rank-one lift is
$$B_s=S\otimes_{\mathbb k[a^2]}S(1)$$
([[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]]); their right origin
reductions are $\mathbb k$ and $C(1)$, whose centered auxiliary degrees are
$-1,1$, and the labels $e^{-1}=e$, $s^{-1}=s$ agree with the dictionary of
[[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]].
Before reduction the standard graph ranks, in the order $(e,s)$, are $(1,0)$
for $B_e$ and $(1,1)$ for $B_s$: in the two-variable model
$B_s=\mathbb k[l,r]/(l^2-r^2)(1)$ the submodule generated by $l-r$ is free of
rank one on the graph $l=-r$ with annihilator $(l+r)$, and the quotient is free of rank one on the graph
$l=r$, with annihilator $(l-r)$
([[def-type-a-standard-graph-bimodules-support-filtrations-and-character]]).
These ranks agree with the Verma-flag multiplicities $(1,0)$ of $P_e$ and
$(1,1)$ of $P_s$ at $v=1$, as predicted by
[[prop-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-standard-filtration-ranks-under-v]]; they
are taken before the graph supports coalesce at the origin, and no grading on
arbitrary category-$\mathcal O$ objects or intrinsic separated-support
filtration on $V(P)$ is asserted.
items.strategy: Use only the named current A-page suppliers and explicit rank-one algebra. In the PBW basis f^n v of M(t), e f^n v=n(t-n+1)f^{n-1}v. At t=0, f v is a singular vector generating M(-2), and the quotient is the one-dimensional L(0); at t=-2 every n>0 coefficient is nonzero, proving simplicity. Highest-weight generation gives nonsplitting of the first sequence. The empty-word case of the projective-generation lemma makes Delta_e=P_e; its one-wall case and the two-step extension lemma give the second sequence and P_s. Since Hom(P_s,L_y) is k for its head y=s and zero for y=e, exactness of V and the displayed composition factors give dimensions 1,2,1,1,0,1 in the stated order. Endomorphismensatz identifies V(P_s) with the regular C-module. The only one-dimensional C-module has x acting by zero, identifying every nonzero dimension-one value with k. Compute Hom_C(k,k)=k, Hom_C(k,C)=kx (annihilator of x), Hom_C(C,k)=k and Hom_C(C,C)=C. Struktursatz with projective targets identifies the four actual O-Hom spaces and compositions; normalize i,p so i(1)=x and p(1)=1, then pi=0 and ip=m_x on the basis 1,x. Independently, the polynomial model for B_s is k[l,r]/(l²-r²)(1). Right reduction r=0 gives k[l]/l²(1). The submodule (l-r) is free rank one on graph l=-r and the quotient is free rank one on graph l=r; the annihilator of l-r is (l+r), since cancellation in k[l,r] is valid. Thus its two standard graph layers have ranks one each. The e lift has only the e graph. Compare the two once-each/one-only Verma flags, invoking the existing multiplicity supplier with total ranks only. The fixed average coordinate in the published two-variable permutation realization is split off and killed on reduction, as explicitly allowed by the existing A-page dictionary. These finite computations illustrate those suppliers, rather than proving their general claims.

items.title: The Soergel functor is not fully faithful on all category-O objects
items.statement:
Assume the inherited Axiom of Choice. In the regular integral
$\mathfrak{sl}_2$ block at $\lambda=0$ (so $\rho=1$ and $s\cdot0=-2$), the
functor $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P(-2),-)$ is fully faithful on
every object of the block, i.e. $V\colon\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(M,N)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VN)$
is a bijection for all objects $M,N$. This is false.
